Action entries retain sanitized kind and fixture path or field identity, selected pane and image paths before and after, trusted pointer events, connectivity, pointer failure, and explicit event truncation.

The existing probe stays armed through each media or link phase, so tab and pointer events between actions can be correlated with the first unexpected Article selection; mutation observation follows pane replacement.

captureMediaFailure stores the shared trace on success or failure and rethrows the original action error; failed teardown is recorded as probeError. No pane reselection or failed-action retry was added.
limits: Phase traces are separate; the interval between warm-media and warm-links, or reload-media and reload-links, is not observed.
The 256-event phase cap and 32-event action cap announce dropped events; a truncated trace cannot establish a complete causal timeline.
The probe itself has not yet been observed in a hosted native run; this is source readiness, not a product pass.

evidence: The patch extends the existing mediaTransitionProbe and native action helpers instead of introducing a parallel observer framework.
ResourceAction still encloses each click and insert; the explicit pre-removal requireResourceHealth remains. The resource boundary implementation and policy were not changed.
New action identities and event targets use fixed fixture paths, labels, fields, and bounded diagnostics; entered text and arbitrary page content are not added to the trace.

limits: Focused tests verify callback and resource-gate wiring, but do not exercise the injected DOM observer or its truncation behavior; the guarded native run is needed to validate those.
A start-probe evaluation failure aborts the attempted action before its resource guard. This is observable as an unverified diagnostic, not a silent resource bypass.
